formMetadata.purpose: Form I-864, Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A of the INA, is filed by a sponsor (typically the petitioner, joint sponsor, substitute sponsor, or 5% owner) to demonstrate that the intending immigrant has adequate means of financial support and is not likely to become a public charge upon admission as a lawful permanent resident.
formMetadata.situations: Required for most family-based immigrant visa and adjustment of status applications under INA §212(a)(4)(C) and §213A, and for certain employment-based cases where a relative filed the I-140 or has 5%+ ownership in the petitioning employer. Required categories include: immediate relatives (IR-1/CR-1, IR-2, IR-5), family preference categories (F-1 through F-4), employment-based cases with relative involvement, and certain special immigrant categories. Exemptions from the I-864 requirement exist for VAWA self-petitioners, widows/widowers, applicants with 40 qualifying quarters, children who will automatically acquire citizenship under INA §320, and categories not subject to INA §212(a)(4) (refugees, asylees, T/U visa holders, SIJs, etc.).
formMetadata.use-cases: 1) U.S. citizen petitioner files I-864 as sponsor for spouse's I-485 concurrent filing. 2) LPR petitioner sponsors adult unmarried child in F-2B category. 3) Joint sponsor (unrelated USC with sufficient income) files when petitioner's income is insufficient. 4) Two joint sponsors each file separate I-864s when one joint sponsor cannot meet requirements alone. 5) Substitute sponsor files when original petitioner has died. 6) Employer with 5%+ relative ownership files I-864 for EB worker. 7) Sponsor uses assets to supplement income (Part 7) when income alone does not meet 125% FPG. 8) Active-duty military petitioner needs only 100% FPG for spouse/child.
formMetadata.filing-context: I-864 is filed with I-485 (adjustment of status) or submitted to the National Visa Center (NVC) for consular processing. Supporting documents include: most recent federal tax return transcript or photocopy (required), up to 3 years of tax returns (optional), proof of citizenship/LPR status, proof of domicile, employment verification (letter, pay stubs, W-2s), and completed I-864A forms from household members contributing income. Must include Form I-864P (Poverty Guidelines) reference. If assets are used, evidence of asset value is required. The sponsor's income must meet 125% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines for household size (100% for active-duty military sponsoring spouse/child). Edition 10/17/24; OMB expires 10/31/2027.
formMetadata.parties-involved: Sponsor: The person signing the I-864, accepting the legally enforceable obligation to financially support the intending immigrant; may be the petitioner, joint sponsor, substitute sponsor, or 5% owner. Principal Immigrant: The primary beneficiary of the underlying immigrant petition. Family Members: Derivative immigrants (spouse/children of principal) being sponsored on the same I-864. Household Members: Persons residing with the sponsor who contribute income via I-864A. Interpreter: Translates the form for the sponsor; Part 9. Preparer: Prepares the form on behalf of the sponsor; Part 10.

fields.description: Part 8, Item 6. Sponsor's Signature. Full certification includes: 'I know the contents of this affidavit of support that I signed; I have read and I understand each of the obligations described in Part 8., and I agree, freely and without any mental reservation or purpose of evasion, to accept each of those obligations in order to make it possible for the immigrant indicated in Part 3. to become a lawful permanent resident of the United States; I agree to submit to the personal jurisdiction of any Federal or state court that has subject matter jurisdiction of a lawsuit against me to enforce my obligations under this Form I-864EZ; Each of the Federal income tax returns submitted in support of this affidavit are true copies, or are unaltered tax transcripts, of the tax returns I filed with the IRS; I understand that, if I am related to the sponsored immigrant by marriage, the termination of the marriage (by divorce, dissolution, annulment, or other legal process) will not relieve me of my obligations under this Form I-864EZ; and I authorize the Social Security Administration to release information about me in its records to the USCIS and DOS.'
fields.notes: Legally binding contract. Creates enforceable obligation to support the immigrant at 125% FPG. Obligation survives divorce. Terminates only upon immigrant's citizenship, 40 quarters, departure with loss of LPR status, new AOS grant, or death of either party.
